title: Notice Bands and the Percentage They Yield on a Cancelled Catering Order
content:
## The bands

The percentage the notice given yields on a pulled order under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement is taken from three bands.

1. **Where notice was given on the service day itself**, the percentage the notice given yields is the same-day percentage printed against the catering service level.
2. **Where the notice given reaches the free-cancellation hours printed against the catering service level**, it yields no percentage at all.
3. **Otherwise**, the percentage the notice given yields is the within-notice percentage printed against the catering service level.

The first band is decided by the day notice was given and the service day the cancellation entry records: notice given on the service day is on that band whatever the hours would otherwise have come to. The second band is decided by the notice given measured in hours against the free-cancellation hours printed against the service level.

## Both sides of the bands

On a hypothetical agreement whose catering service level is printed with free-cancellation hours of 72, a within-notice percentage of 50.0 per cent and a same-day percentage of 100.0 per cent:

| Notice given | Percentage yielded |
| --- | --- |
| Notice given on the service day itself | 100.0 per cent |
| 96 hours | none |
| 72 hours | none |
| 71 hours | 50.0 per cent |
| 24 hours | 50.0 per cent |

Notice of exactly 72 hours reaches the free-cancellation hours of that service level and yields no percentage; notice one hour short of it yields the within-notice percentage.
